subject: Updating R to 3.0.0 & lavaan to 0.5-13 leads to non-definite matrices

messages.author: 32db9d7f15ef6f0b
messages.subject: Updating R to 3.0.0 & lavaan to 0.5-13 leads to non-definite matrices
parts:
Dear all,

I have an odd problem: I updated my installation of R from 2.15 to 3.0.0 and lavaan from o.5-12 to 0.5-13. Afterwards, models that used to fit without problems produce a lavaan WARNING: covariance matrix of latent variables is not positive definite;. use inspect(fit,"cov.lv") to investigate.

This is quite a serious issue for me and I wonder if there is anyone who has observed something similar or has an idea how to fix this? I cannot really share the data set on the internet unfortunately.

Greetings,
Bertolt

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Updating R to 3.0.0 & lavaan to 0.5-13 leads to non-definite matrices
parts:
On 05/28/2013 11:23 AM, Bertolt Meyer wrote:
> Dear all,
>
> I have an odd problem: I updated my installation of R from 2.15 to 3.0.0
> and lavaan from o.5-12 to 0.5-13. Afterwards, models that used to fit
> without problems produce a lavaan WARNING: covariance matrix of latent
> variables is not positive definite;. use inspect(fit,"cov.lv") to
> investigate.

This is a check that has been added in 0.5-11. But perhaps the tolerance
in R 3.0.0 is different from < 3.0.0. The check itself has not changed.

To do the check 'manually', you can do

eigen( inspect(fit,"cov.lv") )$values

if any of the eigenvalues is smaller than zero, the warning pops up.
However, if the value is very close to zero, you are probably still ok.

You can use inspect(fit,"cor.lv") to see the correlation matrix.

I will try to find a way to 'relax' this check a little bit.

Yves.

messages.author: c82e7c65da429d3c
messages.subject: Re: Updating R to 3.0.0 & lavaan to 0.5-13 leads to non-definite matrices
parts:
Yves, thanks for your quick reply. I might indeed have been on a version before 0.5-11. I had a look at the Eigenvalues of the model, and the only negative one was -3.296112e-17. I believe that this is close enough to 0. So maybe the check could indeed be a bit relaxed.

Thanks for your help in clearing this up,
Bertolt
